title: 2005 AMC 10B Problem 18
statement: All of David’s telephone numbers have the form \(555\text{–}abc\text{–}defg,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) \(d,\) \(e,\) \(f,\) and \(g\) are distinct digits and in increasing order, and none is either \(0\) or \(1.\) How many different telephone numbers can David have?

solutions.text:
The seven digits are chosen from \(\{2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9\},\) and once chosen they must be written in increasing order, so only the choice of digits matters.

Choosing seven of these eight digits is the same as choosing the one digit to leave out, which can be done in \(8\) ways.

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: The seven digits come from \(\{2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9\},\) and their order is forced
Once the omitted digit is chosen, every digit’s position in the phone number is determined
